themes.weakness: The insights loop hears almost only from agents building Beeline, not from the people using it.
themes.mechanism: Agents file reports on every refusal; people rarely report. So the ranked list and every theme above measure the build process, while the biggest user drop has no report behind it.

evidence.text: Last week 4 people and 1,433 agent reports; in 30 days 24 human reports from 2 people.
In the last 7 days, 7 of 18 people who signed up never sent a first message.
Of 20 people who signed up in the 7 days to 2026-10-22, 10 sent a message within 24 hours and 1 came back the next day.
The 2026-10-24 walk recorded 1 stuck person; walk history starts that day.
Of 19 people who signed up in the 7 days to 2026-10-23, 11 sent a message within 24 hours and 1 came back the next day (5%).
No human reports since 2026-10-22, against 691 agent reports in the same 3 days.
Of 17 people who signed up in the 7 days to 2026-10-24, 9 sent a message within 24 hours and 1 came back the next day (6%).
No human reports for 4 days (since 2026-10-22), against 1,573 agent reports in the last 7 days.
Paid X ads drew 1,962 link clicks on 2026-10-25, yet Beeline recorded 2 signups in the 24 hours to 09:00 2026-10-26 and no ad-attributed signup. The drop has no report behind it.

Of 17 people who signed up in the 7 days to 2026-10-25, 10 sent a message within 24 hours and 2 came back the next day (12%, up from 6%). Still no human reports since 2026-10-22, against about 1,500 agent reports in 7 days.

Of 18 people who signed up in the 7 days to 2026-10-26, 10 sent a message within 24 hours and 2 came back the next day (11%). The value loop's fixed SQL puts the biggest 28-day loss at the first message: 12 of 21 new outside people never wrote within 24 hours.

Of 16 people who signed up in the 7 days to 2026-10-27, 9 sent a message within 24 hours and 1 came back the next day (6%, down from 11%). Upstream of this, 21 of 29 outside installs that tapped sign-in in 28 days never got in, so the loop hears from even fewer people than the signup count suggests.
Of 14 people who signed up in the 7 days to 2026-10-29, 8 sent a message within 24 hours and 1 came back the next day (7%, from 6% on 2026-10-27).

against: With 19 active people in 28 days, the user data may be too small to show any pattern yet.
themes.prediction: Watching 5 new signups through their first session finds one shared cause for the missing first message.
themes.falsifiedIf: The 5 sessions show 5 unrelated causes, or all send a first message.

themes.weakness: Repeating work (schedules, retries, helper restarts, auto-fix loops) keeps running after a prerequisite is gone, and nothing pauses it.
themes.mechanism: A schedule or loop has no count of identical failures and no rule to stop. It fires on every tick and files a new report each time.

evidence.text: Exact-repeat class: 0.2% of reports in the 7 days to 2026-10-23, 0% the 7 days before. The watchdog words each failure differently, so exact matches miss most of the first-pass repeats.
First pass: one scheduled watchdog with missing files produced 265 reports from 4 agents in 8 Rooms in 30 days, 10% of last week's reports.
One helper start-up error repeated 2,179 times in 14 days.
A CI auto-fix loop woke an agent 6 times during a pause; a weekday schedule fired on Saturday; a monitor ran 8 times without access.
Watchdog reports fell from about 25 a day (2026-10-18 to 2026-10-21) to 1 to 3 a day since 2026-10-23.
The helper start-up repeat stopped after 2026-10-22; no events since.

In a random sample of 250 agent reports (30 days), about 10 are one workspace watchdog failing on the same missing files, each worded differently. The exact-summary track counts none of them, so it undercounts repeats.
A random sample of 250 reports from 30 days shows one scheduled job firing again and again while its required files are missing, filed as a new report each time.
One new person's request hit the free agent time limit 3 times in a row on 2026-10-26 with no result and no change between tries.

against: The watchdog belongs to one workspace's own setup, not to Beeline code.
The 2026-10-25 Sunday pass did not find this as a separate weakness, and both large repeat sources stopped without a general failure budget.
themes.prediction: Pausing a schedule after 3 identical failures and telling its owner cuts these reports by at least 80%.
themes.falsifiedIf: Identical-failure repeats are under 5% of reports once the watchdog setup is fixed.

track.label: Share of reports that repeat the same failure
track.definition: Exact match (scripts/theme-classes.mjs): reports whose identical summary the same reporter filed 3 or more times that Eastern day, as a share of all reports in the 7 days ending that day.

themes.weakness: Gates and agents read copies of pull request, check and brief state that disagree with GitHub and with each other.
themes.mechanism: The merge gate, the checks read, the corner stage and GitHub each hold their own view of the head and its checks. When one lags, an agent is told to act on a state that is no longer true.

evidence.text: Keyword class: 6% of reports in the 7 days to 2026-10-23, up from 2% the 7 days before.
First pass: stale-head, stuck-stage and gate-versus-GitHub reports: 161 in 30 days from 17 agents; 7% of last week's reports, up from 4%.
Unresolved: PR checks HTTP 403 (198 events), check rollup HTTP 502, and a STALE_HEAD verdict rejection.
Ranked problem: done reports refused right after a PR opens, before the corner registers it.
The 2026-10-25 Sunday pass found the same weakness on its own: about 111 gate-versus-GitHub reports in 30 days, 71 of them last week.
On 2026-10-23, 11 merged PRs waited 0.8 to 2.7 hours after all checks were green; after the 2026-10-24 gate fixes the wait fell to minutes.
Keyword class rose to 6.5% of reports in the 7 days to 2026-10-25, from 3.2% on 2026-10-21, more than double the 3% target.
New ranked problem on 2026-10-26: grant approval cards and wakes name old grants while the current one stays pending, 15 reports from 3 agents, continuing after the 2026-10-25 card fix.
New on 2026-10-27: the merge tool reports a closed gate while the checks read reports the merge allowed. Keyword class at 6.3% in the 7 days to 2026-10-26, still about twice the 3% target.

against: Part of this may be GitHub API errors, not divergence.
The 198-event PR checks 403 burst was one night (2026-10-21) and has not recurred.
themes.prediction: In a sample of 50 such reports, at least 30 trace to a stored value that differs from GitHub at the time of the call.
themes.falsifiedIf: Fewer than 20 of 50 sampled reports trace to a stored value that differs from GitHub.

track.label: Share of reports about stale PR and check state
track.definition: Keyword match on the report summary (scripts/theme-classes.mjs): reports naming a stale head, check read or summary, merge or review gate, or a corner or PR not found, as a share of all reports in the 7 days ending that day.

themes.weakness: Each place an agent runs (Room, corner, DM, machine) gives it different tools, files and environment, and the agent learns which only by failing.
themes.mechanism: A Room has no checkout and some apps; a corner has a checkout but may lack gh, the emulator or files from another turn. The prompt does not list what this turn can reach, so agents try, fail and report.

evidence.text: Keyword class: 15% of reports in the 7 days to 2026-10-23, 18% the 7 days before.
First pass: environment reports (gh, emulator, sandbox, grants, checkout, file paths): 411 in 30 days from 22 agents; 14% of last week's reports.
Ranked problems: Android emulator lost in corners; corner-only app tried from a Room.
Android test setup lost between turns cost 2.9 hours last week.
Connected app unavailable in this Room; workflow run unavailable in this Room.
Keyword class: 18% of reports in the 7 days to 2026-10-24, up from 15% the day before.

The 2026-10-25 Sunday pass found two related weaknesses: work environments that do not survive between turns, and ids and approvals that do not resolve across places. Both are candidates that may split from this theme.
Keyword class reached 20% of reports in the 7 days to 2026-10-25, from 11.6% on 2026-10-21, twice the 10% target.
New ranked problem on 2026-10-26: grant requests are refused without naming the missing field, and the approval card size limit has no route from a corner.
Keyword class rose to 21.2% in the 7 days to 2026-10-26, from 11.6% on 2026-10-21; it has risen 5 of the last 6 days.
Two new problems on 2026-10-27 fit it: Room discovery offers corner and app tools that then answer unavailable, and a corner cannot read the working files its brief names.

against: Some environment reports are real infrastructure faults, such as a corrupt repository mirror or out-of-memory restarts.
Part of the rise is one workspace watchdog on another machine repeating the same missing-file failure.
themes.prediction: A capability list given at turn start halves the share of environment reports within 14 days of release.
themes.falsifiedIf: Most sampled environment reports are infrastructure faults that a capability list would not prevent.

track.label: Share of reports about what a place allows
track.definition: Keyword match on the report summary (scripts/theme-classes.mjs): reports naming an emulator, sandbox, grant, checkout, gh, shell, host or a capability unavailable in a Room, as a share of all reports in the 7 days ending that day.

themes.weakness: Tool schemas and descriptions do not state the limits the server enforces, so agents learn the limits by being refused.
themes.mechanism: Length caps, word limits, required pairs of fields and accepted values live in server validators, not in the schema the agent reads. Each refusal costs a retry and often a feedback report.

evidence.text: Keyword class: 14% of reports in the 7 days to 2026-10-23, 14% the 7 days before.
First pass: schema and argument mismatch reports: 396 in 30 days from 19 agents; 14% of last week's reports.
Expected refusals logged as errors: title word limit, one-line ask limit, 16 KB contents limit, brief approval source.
Ranked problem: history search rejects arguments that match its own schema.
Four ranked problems on 2026-10-25 fit: history search arguments, reports to an agent commander, done reports before the PR registers, and brief approval citations.
The 2026-10-25 Sunday pass found the same weakness on its own.
Keyword class flat at 14.2% in the 7 days to 2026-10-25.
Regression on 2026-10-26: the history search fix covered only the limit field; text search and the paging cursor are still refused.

History and memory search still refuse arguments without naming the allowed values: 7 reports from 3 agents, after a fix that covered only one field. Keyword class at 13.5% in the 7 days to 2026-10-26, flat.

against: Some refusals are correct, and the agent ignored a limit the schema does state.
themes.prediction: Generating schema limits from the server validators removes these Sentry rows and halves the share of mismatch reports.
themes.falsifiedIf: In a sample of 50 mismatch reports, most limits were already stated in the schema.

track.label: Share of reports about unstated tool limits
track.definition: Keyword match on the report summary (scripts/theme-classes.mjs): reports naming a schema, argument, parameter, limit, documented or advertised behavior, or a rejected call, as a share of all reports in the 7 days ending that day.

themes.weakness: Beeline sends wakes and review dispatches from single signals, without knowing what already happened or who caused it.
themes.mechanism: Each event source (checks, orders, brief revisions, merges, idle timers) wakes agents on its own. None checks whether the work already moved on, so agents get duplicate, stale or wrongly classed wakes.

evidence.text: Keyword class: 24% of reports in the 7 days to 2026-10-23, up from 16% the 7 days before.
First pass: wake and dispatch reports: 458 in 30 days from 19 agents in 184 Rooms; 17% of last week's reports, 16% the week before.
Cases include duplicate reviewer dispatch on an unchanged head, own brief revisions classed as human, false unreported-order alerts and false idle-corner alerts.
Reviewer not woken after green checks cost 2.6 hours last week.
Recent merges each patch one case: #2886, #2898, #2907, #2908.
Keyword class: 23% of reports in the 7 days to 2026-10-24, still about twice the target.
Two fixes did not hold after release: wakes still stop running turns (after #2892) and review handoffs still repeat on an unchanged head (after #2907).
The 2026-10-25 Sunday pass, without this folder, found the same weakness on its own and rated it high.
Keyword class at 21.6% in the 7 days to 2026-10-25, down from 23.0%; the stale-wake-drop experiment went live on 2026-10-26.
The repeated-review handoff came back 6 hours after its second fix shipped on 2026-10-25.

Keyword class at 20.7% in the 7 days to 2026-10-26, down from 21.6%. Since the stale-wake-drop change went live, 6.5% of 107 reports are about wakes; the review handoff on an unchanged head came back again on 2026-10-27 after its third per-case fix.

against: Some reports may be one bug reported many times by the same corner.
themes.prediction: Per-case fixes will not lower the share of wake reports below 12% in the next 14 days.
themes.falsifiedIf: The wake-report share falls below 8% by 2026-11-07 with only per-case fixes merged.

track.label: Share of reports about wakes and dispatch
track.definition: Keyword match on the report summary (scripts/theme-classes.mjs): reports naming a wake, dispatch, idle-corner alert or unreported order, as a share of all reports in the 7 days ending that day.
